title: Charlotte historian says historians under threat | Community | vtcng.com
text:
Bill Fox, a Charlotte resident and trained historian, worries that “history and historians are under threat” from certain powerful politicians. Speaking about his new book, “Envoy to the Archives: Ruth Anna Fisher and Hidden Transatlantic History,” at the Charlotte Public Library recently, he cited what he considers abuses against the profession, including President Donald Trump’s early dismissal of the nation’s archivist and the appointment of Marco Rubio as a replacement.
The book tells the story of Ruth Anna Fisher, a Black archivist and the daughter of a formerly enslaved person. Fisher knew W.E.B. Du Bois, Booker T. Washington and other prominent figures on both sides of the Atlantic. She helped transform the field of U.S. historical documentation but received insufficient recognition for her achievements during the Jim Crow era. Fox’s book seeks to address that oversight.
